name: Revenant
body:
Beyond the veil that separates life from death, where spirits linger and the echoes of the past whisper, the revenants walk a solitary path. These beings, once dead and now returned, are driven by an indomitable will to complete unfinished business that anchors them to the mortal realm.

Revenants are the embodiment of resolve and purpose, their presence a testament to the power of the human spirit to transcend even death itself.

The creation of a revenant is always born of a profound emotional or spiritual turmoil – a grave injustice, a betrayal, an unfulfilled promise. This intense focus and connection to their unfinished task grant revenants their unique abilities, but also curse them with a restless existence until their purpose is achieved. Once their mission is complete, they believe, peace will finally be theirs.

Habitat

Revenants have no need for a home, as their habitat is wherever their unfinished business leads them. They are often found haunting the places significant to their past lives or quests, whether those be ancient ruins, battlefields stained with their blood, or the bustling streets of cities where their final deeds must be carried out. To a revenant, the world is not a place to live but a realm to traverse in pursuit of closure.

Appearance

To behold a revenant is to see the visage of determination and sorrow made flesh. These beings retain the appearance they had in life, though marked by the passage through death.

Their bodies are often pale, their eyes glowing with a spectral light that betrays their supernatural nature. Despite their ghostly appearance, revenants are very much corporeal, bound to the physical world until their purpose is fulfilled. Revenants move with a purposeful grace, their actions deliberate and their focus unwavering. They speak rarely, and when they do, their voices carry the weight of their unresolved mission. The air around them might grow colder, or objects might move slightly – subtle signs of their connection to the realm of the dead.

Abilities and Powers

Revenants are granted powers that aid them in their quest for resolution. They possess an unnatural resilience, able to recover from wounds that would kill a normal person. Their determination grants them immunity to being frightened, and they can sense the presence of those who have wronged them or stand in the way of their objectives, no matter the distance.

Moreover, revenants can sometimes manifest abilities that reflect the nature of their unfinished business – strength to right a wrong, the power to protect what was once lost, or the means to uncover long-buried truths. These abilities are as varied, each uniquely suited to the task that binds the revenant to the world of the living.

Interaction with Other Races

Revenants are solitary figures, their existence focused entirely on the completion of their tasks.

They form no lasting bonds, and their interactions with others are often brief and purpose-driven. To the living, a revenant can be a figure of fear and awe – a reminder of the power of the unresolved and the lengths to which the spirit will go to find peace. Yet, some revenants become legends, their quests for redemption or vengeance becoming stories told across generations. In these tales, the revenants are both warning and inspiration, embodying the idea that some bonds cannot be broken by death, and some duties are too important to be left unfinished. Despite their isolation, revenants can become unexpected allies, drawn into the world of the living by their vengeful quest.

Revenant Traits

Emerging from the shadow of death, Revenants are bound to the mortal world by a cause left unfulfilled. These traits stem from their relentless pursuit to accomplish what anchors them between realms, showcasing their tenacity and supernatural resilience. While playing as a Revenant, you gain the following racial traits:

Ability Score Increase. The ordeal of returning from the dead bestows upon you a hardiness of form and a force of personality. Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.
Age. The passage of time ceases to hold sway over you. Revenants persist in the condition they were revived, un-aging and locked in their moment of return until their purpose reaches its conclusion.
Alignment. The singular focus of a Revenant often aligns them towards a path of neutrality, their moral compass directed by the quest that binds them to the living world. Yet, the nature of their quest can sway them across the spectrum of alignment.
Size. The physical stature of a Revenant mirrors their form in life, usually standing within the medium range of height and build. Your size is Medium.
Speed. With a base walking speed of 30 feet, your movements are driven by the urgency of your mission, unhindered by the weight of mortality.
Languages. The knowledge of tongues remains from your life, allowing you to speak, read, and write Common and one additional language known to you before your death.
Unfinished Business. A deep-seated compulsion to resolve your lingering task empowers you. When acting in direct pursuit of this goal, you can choose to gain advantage on any ability check, attack roll, or saving throw you make. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining any expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Relentless Endurance. When damage would reduce you to 0 hit point but not kill your outright, you can choose to drop at 1 hit point instead. After you use this ability, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.
Deathly Determination. Your spirit’s fortification against the ethereal influences grants you advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened, a testament to your ordeal through death’s domain.
Ethereal Sight. The veil between planes now partially lifted for you, you have the ability to gaze into the Ethereal Plane out to a range of 60 feet.
Vengeful Tracker. Your revenant nature grants you the supernatural ability to track those you seek vengeance upon. You always know the direction and distance of any creature against which you seek revenge, even if the creatures and you are on different planes of existence. If the creature being tracked by you dies, you know.
The Revenant Lineage as a Narrative Device

Incorporating the Revenant lineage into your campaign offers a compelling narrative device, especially when considering the return of a deceased character for the climax of your story. This approach is particularly useful in scenarios where traditional resurrection is unavailable or undesired, adding a layer of depth and emotional resonance to the campaign’s final sessions.

Playing as a revenant allows for a deceased character to return with a singular, driving purpose, adding urgency and focus to the campaign’s conclusion. This character, now bound by the relentless pursuit of their unfinished business, brings not only their personal quest for resolution but also a poignant reminder of the stakes at play. It enriches the narrative by providing a direct, personal connection to the overarching themes and conflicts of your story.

The revenant’s time-limited existence underscores the fleeting opportunity for the party to rectify past mistakes, achieve mutual goals, or confront a shared enemy. It adds a layer of tension and dramatic weight to the campaign, as the party must navigate their final challenges.

Moreover, this inclusion allows for a meaningful exploration of themes such as redemption, sacrifice, and the impact of loss, enhancing the emotional depth of your campaign’s resolution, while also offering the players a unique opportunity to reflect on their journey, the choices they’ve made, and the bonds they’ve forged, all while racing against time to help their revenant companion find peace.

Becoming a Revenant

The transition from mortal to revenant is not a path that many can walk. It is a transformation born of unresolved conflict, unyielding will, and often, profound tragedy. A character may become a revenant through various means, each deeply personal and unique to the individual’s story. Some examples are detailed below.

Unfinished Business: The most common way to become a revenant is through dying with a significant task left incomplete. This task must be deeply important to the character, such as avenging a wrongful death, protecting a loved one from imminent danger, or completing a vital mission that was cruelly cut short by death.

Divine Intervention: A deity or powerful entity might intervene at the moment of the character’s death, granting them the chance to return as a revenant. This usually occurs when the character’s mission aligns with the deity’s interests or serves a greater purpose within the cosmic balance.

Cursed Existence: A powerful curse placed upon the character at the moment of their death could prevent their soul from passing on, forcing them back into the mortal realm to fulfill a condition set by the curse. Breaking such a curse often involves a quest of redemption, vengeance, or purification.

Magical Experimentation: In rare cases, a character might become a revenant through magical means, such as a necromantic experiment gone awry or a failed attempt at resurrection. These revenants often struggle with their identity, caught between the realms of the living and the dead.

Voluntary Sacrifice: A character might willingly choose to become a revenant to protect something or someone of great importance. This self-sacrifice requires a ritual in which the character pledges their soul to their cause, returning from death with the powers of a revenant to fulfill their pledge.

Natural Phenomenon: Occasionally, powerful magical phenomena can cause the spontaneous creation of revenants. This might occur in places where the veil between life and death is thin, such as ancient battlefields, cursed lands, or sites of great tragedy.

Exacting your Vengeance

As a revenant, you are granted one year from the moment of your reanimation to exact vengeance on those who wronged you or to complete your unfinished business. This time is marked by an internal clock known only to you, counting down the days until your quest must be fulfilled.

If you succeed in exacting your vengeance or completing your task before the year is up, you find peace. Your soul is released from its earthly bonds, allowing you to pass on to the afterlife or be reincarnated, according to the cosmology of the world you inhabit. This transition is often accompanied by a sense of fulfillment and a final moment of clarity, where the significance of your actions and their impact on the world are revealed to you.

If you fail to achieve your objective within the allotted time, the curse that binds you to the mortal realm consumes you. Your form dissipates into nothingness, your soul lost to the ether. This not only represents a failure to accomplish what you returned for but also the obliteration of your essence, preventing reincarnation or any form of afterlife. The remnants of your being are scattered across the planes, serving as a warning to others about the cost of unfinished business and the relentless march of time.
